initial_symptoms: container uptimes inconsistent across the stack (redis2, go-server didn't match the rest)
redis_evicted_keys_total flat at 0 for 28 minutes then jumping to ~70000 and climbing
redis_memory_used_bytes collapsing from a steadily-growing 8.47MB to 5.21MB and pinning there
pipeline throughput otherwise looked entirely healthy
investigation_path: get_container_state -> all running, but uptime anomalies flagged for explanation
list_recent_changes(3h) -> every fault paired inject/restore except redis/02_eviction_storm, injected 15:33:49 with no restore
get_metrics(redis_evicted_keys_total, 30m) -> flat at 0 until 15:33:59 (10s after injection), then climbing continuously - verified independently rather than trusting the changelog alone
read_config(redis1) -> maxmemory=5242880 (5MiB), maxmemory-policy=allkeys-lru
read_config(redis2), read_config(redis3) -> both at cluster defaults (maxmemory=0, noeviction) - confirmed redis1 is the sole outlier, not the baseline design
query_logs(go-server) -> clean ingest, zero errors, ruled out the front of the pipeline
get_metrics(kafka_consumergroup_lag, 30m) -> healthy sawtooth unchanged after the injection - ruled out throughput/backpressure damage
get_metrics(redis_memory_used_bytes, 30m) -> climbed to 8.47MB then collapsed to 5.21MB at 15:34:18, pinned at the exact maxmemory ceiling
read_config(go-enricher) -> ruled out an earlier unrelated fault (pool size) leaving residue
query_logs(redis1, 20m) -> Redis's own warning: CONFIG SET maxmemory 5242880 was below current usage of 8492104, forcing eviction; BGSAVE key counts collapsing 2484 -> 406
root_cause: A CONFIG SET at 15:33:49 dropped redis1's maxmemory to 5MiB, below its live ~8.5MB working set, under an allkeys-lru policy - forcing continuous eviction of that shard's keys to stay under the cap. Fraud-tracking state (per-IP velocity/count, stored under fraud:{ip}) lives on whatever shard owns that hash slot, so this is a silent correctness failure (under-counted velocity, false negatives) rather than a throughput or error-rate incident - every standard health signal (ingest, consumer lag) reads green.
verified_against_code: go-enricher/redis_functions.go:136-146 (updateFraudInRedis persists per-IP fraud state to key fraud:{ip} via Lua script) confirms evicted keys are real fraud-tracking state, not a disposable cache; read_config(redis1) independently reproduced the exact maxmemory=5242880/allkeys-lru values; redis-cli INFO stats independently confirmed evicted_keys climbing
tool_bug_found: query_logs crashed with a NoneType error on go-enricher specifically - root cause was subprocess text-mode decoding with the Windows default codepage (cp1252) instead of UTF-8, which threw on a non-cp1252 byte in the container's log output. Fixed in mcp-server/server.py by forcing encoding='utf-8', errors='replace' in _run_compose() and the docker inspect call in read_config.

initial_symptoms: redis2 container in exited state, clean stop (exit code 0), not a crash
transaction throughput collapsed from a steady ~4.2 tx/s to ~0
kafka_consumergroup_lag dropped to exactly 0 on all 3 partitions simultaneously - the opposite of a stalled-consumer signature
investigation_path: get_container_state -> redis2 exited(0) ~1m ago, other services recently restarted from earlier unrelated faults
list_recent_changes(3h) -> every fault paired inject/restore except redis/01_node_stopped, injected 16:09:04 with no restore
query_logs(go-server, ERROR, 20m) -> one stale Kafka connect error from ~15:52, ruled out as the current cause
read_config(redis1, redis3) -> both at maxmemory=0/noeviction baseline, ruled out lingering residue from the earlier eviction-storm fault
get_metrics(redis_evicted_keys_total, 45m) -> flat since ~15:43, confirmed eviction storm genuinely over and not the current cause
get_metrics(kafka_consumergroup_lag, 30m) -> exactly 0 on all partitions from ~16:09:30 - zero lag at the moment of collapse pointed at a producer stall, not slow consumers
get_metrics(rate(fraud_server_transactions_total[1m]), 30m) -> steady ~4.2 tx/s collapsing to ~0 at 16:09:41

get_metrics same query over 80m as a control -> the earlier node_stopped injection (15:01-15:06) produced an identical collapse to ~0 that recovered exactly on restore, while the eviction storm and kafka scale-down faults never produced this signature - established Redis node loss as uniquely reproducing a full pipeline stall
query_logs(go-server, grep='redis|cluster', 15m) -> dial failures to 192.168.241.101 plus explicit 'CLUSTERDOWN The cluster is down'
read_config(go-server) -> REDIS_CLUSTER_ADDRS confirmed .101 as the middle cluster address, ruled out residue from the earlier pool-size fault
read_config(redis2) -> confirmed service not running, .101 mapped to the actually-down node
list_recent_changes(20m) -> reconfirmed the fault was still un-restored at conclusion time
root_cause: redis/01_node_stopped took down redis2 (192.168.241.101). The cluster runs 3 masters with zero replicas and cluster-require-full-coverage=yes (the unmodified Redis default), so losing any single node leaves its hash slots unowned and trips CLUSTERDOWN for the entire cluster - not just keys that would have hashed to the dead node. Every dedup/rate-limit lookup in go-server's SendTransaction path fails with CLUSTERDOWN, stalling ingest to ~0 tx/s. The fault is a total, cluster-wide outage from a single node loss, not a partial degradation, because there is no replica to fail over to and full coverage is required.
verified_against_code: go-server/server.go:72-79 (Redis Dedup check, matches the exact log format 'WARNING: Some issue with Redis Dedup check: {err}' seen in real logs); redis-cli CONFIG GET cluster-require-full-coverage on redis1 independently confirmed 'yes'; go-server logs independently confirmed the literal CLUSTERDOWN error text
note: this is the second, properly-run attempt at this fault (Opus, max effort, standardized prompt) - the first attempt was built ad-hoc before the corpus protocol was finalized and was discarded. The redo surfaced a more precise mechanism (cluster-wide CLUSTERDOWN via cluster-require-full-coverage) than the discarded attempt's explanation (only redis2's own slots failing), which also better matches the observed total throughput collapse rather than a partial one.

query_logs(go-enricher, 20m unfiltered) -> normal enrichment/publishing activity, confirmed alive and current

get_metrics({__name__=~'fraud.*'}) full reconciliation -> per-replica processed rates summed to match total input rate; errors_total{reason=unmarshal}=1 on exactly two replicas, flat; all other error counters flat - ruled out message loss or an ongoing error; correctly identified the flatlined go-enricher:9101 series as a stale/abandoned scrape target rather than a stalled consumer

query_logs(go-enricher, since=fault injection timestamp) -> exactly one Failed to Unmarshal postdating 18:48:20Z - tied the error directly to this injection

query_logs(go-enricher, 3h, grep 'Failed to Unmarshal') -> exactly two occurrences total, matching the two malformed-event injections run today (16:36:40 and 18:48:20) - confirmed one poison message per injection, not a continuous stream
query_logs(kafka, level=ERROR) -> no matches - ruled out a broker-side fault
list_recent_changes(20m) re-check -> fault still open, confirmed at conclusion time
root_cause: An un-restored kafka/08_malformed_event injection at 18:48:20Z placed a single non-protobuf message on raw_transactions. go-enricher-2's proto.Unmarshal call failed on it, incremented fraud_enricher_errors_total{reason='unmarshal'} by 1, and the poison message was dropped - not retried, not blocking its partition. Blast radius is negligible: one bad message out of ~254,000, no lag buildup, no throughput impact, no cascading failure. This is the fault behaving exactly as designed - a single dropped message, not a sustained pipeline problem.
verified_against_code: go-enricher/enricher.go:119-123 (proto.Unmarshal call, 'Failed to Unmarshal' print, enricherErrorsTotal.WithLabelValues('unmarshal').Inc() - exact match to observed log text and metric label); independently queried Prometheus query_range across the restart window and confirmed the 'stalled consumer' red herring was genuinely a frozen dead time series (climbed steadily then froze at exactly 25837 the instant Prometheus stopped scraping the old single-replica target), matching Claude's claim exactly rather than being a plausible-sounding guess
note: This trial ran in a genuinely clean environment (correct protocol: Opus, max effort, standardized prompt; no leftover un-restored faults or host-side testing residue, unlike the first fault-8 attempt which was discarded). It also correctly navigated a real, unplanned red herring: a frozen zombie metric series left over from a same-day Prometheus scrape-config fix (see Step 15's multi-replica scrape gap), correctly ruling it out as unrelated to the current fault rather than being misled by it, and correctly inferred that this frozen metric was likely the actual reason 'something seemed off' in the first place - a genuinely sophisticated piece of reasoning volunteered without being asked.

initial_symptoms: throughput collapse on go-server: fraud_server_transactions_total fell from steady ~4.0 tx/s to ~0.94 tx/s (-76%)
p95 transaction latency on go-server jumped from ~8ms to ~975ms (~120x)
kafka_consumergroup_lag fell to 0 across all partitions - counterintuitive for a slowdown, actually indicating upstream starvation not health
zero error lines anywhere in any service's logs
investigation_path: get_container_state -> all running, redis2 uptime flagged as an anomaly to explain (later resolved as benign, leftover from an earlier already-restored fault)
list_recent_changes(6h) -> 27 entries, all paired except network/09_latency_injection at 19:06:05Z with no restore - ruled in an active fault, gave a precise correlation timestamp
get_metrics(kafka_consumergroup_lag) -> flat 0-10, trending to 0 - initially looks healthy but correctly interpreted as starvation once combined with the throughput evidence
get_metrics(rate(fraud_server_transactions_total[1m])) -> steady ~4.0/s collapsing to ~0.93/s starting 19:06:23Z, ~18s after the injection
get_metrics discovery query after an initial wrong metric-name guess -> found the correct fraud_server_*/fraud_enricher_* metric families
get_metrics p95 fraud_server_transaction_duration_seconds_bucket -> ~8ms flat, then climbing to ~975ms from 19:06:26Z
get_metrics p95 fraud_enricher_message_duration_seconds_bucket -> flat ~4.9ms throughout, including after the injection - localized the fault specifically to go-server's path, not the enricher's
query_logs(go-server, 15m) and grep for error/timeout/deadline/refused/retry across go-server and go-enricher -> no matches anywhere - confirmed pure added delay, not a failure mode
get_metrics error-rate counters (rate_limit_error, redis_dedup, unmarshal) -> all flat at 0 - confirmed nothing is failing, ruled out lingering effects from earlier unrelated faults
read_config(go-server) -> REDIS_POOL_SIZE unset/default - ruled out the earlier pool-size fault as a contributing cause
get_metrics(redis_instantaneous_eventloop_duration_usec) -> 200-800 microseconds, statistically unchanged - ruled out Redis server-side processing as the source, proving the ~1s delay is on the wire
read_config(redis1) -> maxmemory=0/noeviction/maxclients=10000 baseline - ruled out the earlier eviction-storm fault as a contributing cause
list_recent_changes(45m) re-check -> fault still active, confirmed at conclusion time
query_logs(python-producer, grep drop/block/queue/retry) -> no matches - confirmed transactions are being delayed, not dropped, upstream of go-server
root_cause: network/09_latency_injection added ~200ms of tc netem delay to go-server's outbound network interface. Because SendTransaction makes multiple sequential blocking round trips (Redis dedup SetNX, rate-limit Lua script, Kafka produce), the per-packet delay compounds additively per request, producing ~1s of added p95 latency and serializing throughput down to ~1 tx/s. Zero errors anywhere because nothing is failing - everything is just slow. The enricher's own processing latency is completely unaffected (flat ~4.9ms), correctly isolating the fault to go-server's network path specifically rather than a shared downstream dependency like Redis or Kafka.
verified_against_code: independently reproduced the p95 measurement directly against Prometheus (measured ~954ms, matching Claude's reported ~975ms); independently confirmed redis_instantaneous_eventloop_duration_usec is a real exported metric currently reading 294 microseconds, matching the claimed 200-800us range
note: This is the fault catalog's designated 'highest-value' fault (per the project's own docs: produces no error lines anywhere, purely a metrics-histogram shift). The investigation correctly avoided the natural misread of 'low Kafka lag = healthy' by combining it with throughput evidence to correctly conclude starvation instead, and used a precise differential technique (comparing per-service latency histograms) to localize the fault to exactly one hop rather than guessing.
tool_bug_found: get_metrics had no cap on the number of returned time series (only on datapoints per series), so a broad/discovery-style query (e.g. matching all metric names) could return multi-megabyte responses - reproduced directly: an unscoped query returned 2.7MB, which triggered an MCP client-side size warning during this investigation. Fixed by adding a MAX_SERIES=25 cap with a clear truncation notice, mirroring query_logs's existing MAX_LOG_LINES pattern. Verified the fix collapses the same query to ~20KB with a clear 'showing first 25 of 2503' notice, and confirmed normal single-series queries are unaffected.

initial_symptoms: go-server in state=paused while every other container is running/healthy
fraud_server_transactions_total collapsed from steady ~4.0 tx/s and the metric series stops entirely rather than continuing at a low value
kafka_consumergroup_lag pinned at exactly 0 on all partitions, after normally fluctuating 0-15 - counterintuitive since a frozen service usually implies backlog
go-server logs end abruptly with no error, panic, or shutdown message
python-producer logs stop mid-transaction: generates a sample but never logs the corresponding Sent line
investigation_path: get_container_state -> go-server: state=paused, only anomaly in an otherwise all-running stack
list_recent_changes(6h) -> 29 entries, all paired except network/11_container_paused at 19:16:54Z with no restore - ruled in the active fault, ruled out all 6 other same-day faults as closed out

get_metrics(rate(fraud_server_transactions_total[1m]), 1h) -> distinguished the CURRENT collapse (series terminating) from an EARLIER, already-restored latency-injection dip (~0.94 tx/s that fully recovered to ~4.05 tx/s afterward) - correctly avoided conflating two different faults' symptoms from the same day

get_metrics(kafka_consumergroup_lag, 1h) -> flat at 0 on all partitions from 19:17:04 onward, still reporting past go-server's last sample - reasoned that a frozen CONSUMER produces climbing lag, so zero lag means the message SOURCE stopped, not a consumer stalling - correctly distinguished this from fault 5's opposite signature

query_logs(go-server, 20m) -> continuous normal activity ending abruptly with no error/panic/shutdown line - ruled out crash, OOM, and graceful shutdown; identified the clean mid-stream cutoff as the SIGSTOP signature specifically

query_logs(python-producer, 6m) -> last successful Sent line exactly matches go-server's final processed transaction (same user ID, same amount) at sub-second precision, then a new sample generated immediately after with no Sent line ever appearing - proved the producer is blocked mid-gRPC-call on a frozen server (SIGSTOP keeps the socket open, so the client hangs instead of getting connection-refused), and proved zero data was lost in flight
query_logs(go-enricher, 15m, ERROR) -> no matches - ruled out enricher failure, correctly attributed their idleness to starvation from the frozen producer rather than their own fault
read_config(redis1) -> baseline maxmemory=0/noeviction/maxclients=10000 - ruled out lingering effects from the earlier eviction-storm fault

read_config(go-enricher) -> REDIS_POOL_SIZE unset/default, and KAFKA_CONSUMER_TOPICS_ENRICHER=raw_transactions independently confirmed go-enricher is the consumer and go-server is the producer - corroborated the direction-of-flow reasoning used to interpret the zero-lag signal
root_cause: network/11_container_paused froze go-server via SIGSTOP at 19:16:54Z. Because go-server is the producer into raw_transactions (not a consumer), freezing it stops the message source entirely rather than creating a backlog - hence kafka_consumergroup_lag goes to exactly zero rather than climbing, the opposite signature from a frozen/scaled-down consumer (fault 5). The frozen process keeps its TCP socket open, so python-producer's in-flight gRPC call hangs indefinitely instead of failing with connection-refused, and no data is lost - the transaction in flight at freeze time was fully processed before the freeze took effect.
verified_against_code: independently read go-server's and python-producer's raw container logs directly and confirmed the exact cross-service match Claude claimed: go-server's final line and python-producer's final Sent line both show user 92819302-1d63-4d5e-a04d-2d8e9a734c20, amount 6775.65, and confirmed the next producer sample (timestamp 19:16:54.538982) has no corresponding Sent line - the hung-call claim is exactly correct, not a plausible-sounding guess
note: This is the cleanest demonstration yet of the fault catalog's core design principle (see faults_and_descriptions.md: several faults look identical from the outside and must be told apart via evidence). The investigation explicitly contrasted this fault's zero-lag signature against a stalled-consumer's climbing-lag signature (fault 5's mechanism) using direction-of-flow reasoning confirmed independently via read_config, rather than pattern-matching 'throughput dropped' to a single default explanation.
